Definition: probably from the base of G3145 (through the idea of contact); a whip (literally, the Roman flagellum for criminals; figuratively, a disease):--plague, scourging.
BiblicalUsage: mástix is a whip, the Roman flagellum, and figuratively a plague or affliction. In Acts 22:24 Paul is to be examined by scourging, and in Hebrews 11:36 the faithful have trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, with bonds and imprisonment. In Luke 7:21 and Mark 3:10 the same word names the plagues and infirmities Jesus cures, as the crowds press to touch Him. The word is the stroke that wounds and the affliction that needs healing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mástix shows me that a whip can be a plague and a plague can be a whip. I hold that the God who heals the plagued is the God who bore the scourging.
